AuditoryStimulus.description:
The tone sweep's pips (src/sounds/pips.bin), each equalised for its speaker: on every rig.yml speaker where the
picked initial azimuth is "all", else on rig.yml's speaker nearest it at elevationDeg.

levelDbfs.description: The tone sweep's pips's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default -55. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

elevationDeg.description: Elevation the sound plays at, in degrees: with the azimuth drawn, it picks rig.yml's nearest speaker
elevationDeg.title: ElevationDeg

initialAzimuthsDeg.description: Where the pips play, one picked per trial: "all" on every rig.yml speaker at once (the corridor's sound, logged auditoryInitialAzimuthDeg NaN with a level); a signed azimuth in degrees (positive right, 0 the centre) on rig.yml's speaker nearest it at elevationDeg, logged as that speaker's auditoryInitialAzimuthDeg and auditoryElevationDeg. Unused where the level is mute
initialAzimuthsDeg.title: InitialAzimuthsDeg

AuditoryStimulus.title: AuditoryStimulus

Curriculum.description:
The Mouse Curriculum stage the values came from, and the task file's only record of the stage: filled by app-rig-control
at launch; empty in the repo's task files. Bonsai only records it.

id.description: The stage's id in the curriculum, fixed and hidden: never shown to the experimenter
id.title: Id

code.description: The stage's code in the curriculum, S then two digits then a capital letter (S03A)
code.title: Code

version.description: The stage's version, 4 characters from abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789 (k7f2)
version.title: Version

path.description: The stage's path in the curriculum, one capital letter (A)
path.title: Path

label.description: The stage's label in the curriculum
label.title: Label

sha256.description: The sha256 of the curriculum file's text app-rig-control ran it from
sha256.title: Sha256

Curriculum.title: Curriculum

OptogeneticsSettings.description:
Zapit optogenetic stimulation: the lab's block (open_rigs.core.task Optogenetics) and this task's laser timing.

The stimulation sites and ramp-down are set in the Zapit conditions file loaded in Zapit, not here; Bonsai reads
the same file to list its conditions and its max ramp-down. "Stimulus" is the tone and grating; the laser is
continuous: it starts at the trigger (the trigger line's rising edge on a hardware-triggered rig), laser_to_stimulus_seconds
before the first tone pip (after it if negative), in whole 50 ms steps and at most 0.2 s, and Bonsai stops it at the
trial's outcome, or at a cap derived at Go (the max stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds plus responseWindowSeconds any condition can draw plus
laser_to_stimulus_seconds plus 0.25 s) if that comes first. The trigger line, and the masking light on it, stays high past
the outcome for the conditions file's max ramp-down. A trial that ends before its trigger has no laser.

enabled.description: Whether this is an optogenetics experiment, Zapit running it: every trial sends it a condition from the conditions file (laser off at 0 mW on laser-off trials: the galvos move and the masking light shows), and the launching app checks Zapit is answering before Go
enabled.title: Enabled

zapitConditionsPath.description: Path to the Zapit conditions file loaded in Zapit. Its top-level stimLocations01, stimLocations02, ... entries are the conditions, numbered 1 to N with no gaps. The launching app keeps a copy beside the task file at Go
zapitConditionsPath.title: ZapitConditionsPath

laserPowerMw.description: Laser power on laser-on trials, in mW, the same for every condition: sent to Zapit with each StartStimulus (overriding the conditions file's power; Zapit's laser calibration turns it into volts) and logged as laserPowerMw (0 on laser-off trials). Required with optogenetics on
laserPowerMw.title: LaserPowerMw

laserOnProbability.description: Probability that a trial after trialsBeforeLaser is a laser-on trial, shared equally by every condition in the conditions file; all other trials are laser-off trials, sent a condition with the laser off
laserOnProbability.title: LaserOnProbability

laserToStimulusSeconds.description: Signed, in seconds: the trigger (the ZapitTrigger line) comes this long before the stimulus; 0 with it; negative after it. The trial's start is the end of the interval less the lead, max(this, 0), once the quiet waits hold, and the stimulus comes the lead after the trial's start in every experiment, optogenetics on or off, so timing never reveals Zapit; the trigger only with optogenetics. Zapit is armed during the interval and adds no time. Refused above itiMinSeconds - 0.2 s (Zapit's reply margin); each task adds its own limits
laserToStimulusSeconds.title: LaserToStimulusSeconds

trialsBeforeLaser.description: Trials at the experiment's start with no laser-on trial among them (each still sends Zapit a condition, at 0 mW); laserOnProbability applies from the next trial
trialsBeforeLaser.title: TrialsBeforeLaser

OptogeneticsSettings.title: OptogeneticsSettings

Penalty.description:
What a penalised trial costs, by its kind (OpenRigs.Trials Penalties.For): incorrect (a wrong choice, a go/no-go
false alarm, a probe's tails) or noResponse (a miss), each its own full values, nothing inherited. noResponse null:
misses are never penalised, and a task that penalises one refuses it at Go (check_misses). Which trials are penalised,
and of which kind, is the task's.

incorrect.description: What a penalised wrong choice costs (a go/no-go false alarm, a probe's tails)
incorrect.title: Incorrect

noResponse.description: What a penalised miss costs; null: misses are never penalised (refused at Go by a task that penalises one)
noResponse.title: NoResponse

Penalty.title: Penalty

PenaltyCost.description:
What one kind of penalised outcome costs: its timeout (the trial log's penaltyTimeoutSeconds), the penalty sound and
the penalty flash (penaltyFlashBrightness).

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout after the penalised outcome, in seconds; the next interval starts after it
timeoutSeconds.title: TimeoutSeconds

sound.description: The penalty sound, with the timeout
sound.title: Sound

flash.description: The penalty flash, with the sound; off (brightness 0) by default
flash.title: Flash

PenaltyCost.title: PenaltyCost

PenaltyFlash.description:
The penalty flash (OpenRigs.Vision PlayPenaltyFlash, the same in every task with a projector): the whole projector
field at brightness of full white, flashing at rateHz from the outcome for the penalty sound's length, which must fit in
the kind's timeout (checked at Go against the sound file, OpenRigs.Trials PenaltyFlashRules, the same rules).

brightness.description: Brightness of the flash, 0 to 1 of the projector's full white after gamma correction (1: full white), over the whole field and everything drawn, a stimulus still on included; 0: no flash (as the sound's mute). Logged as penaltyFlashBrightness
brightness.title: Brightness

rateHz.description: Flash rate in Hz: the field is white for the first half of each 1/rateHz cycle and the normal display the other half, from the outcome for the penalty sound's length (refused at Go when longer than timeoutSeconds); at most 30, half the projector's 60 Hz render loop
rateHz.title: RateHz

PenaltyFlash.title: PenaltyFlash

PenaltySound.description:
The lab's penalty sound (OpenRigs.Audio PlayPenaltySound, the same in every task), on rig.yml's speakerArray.penaltySoundChannel alone,
equalised for that speaker, at each penalised trial's levelDbfs.

levelDbfs.description: The penalty sound's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default -35. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

PenaltySound.title: PenaltySound

Reward.description:
Reward delivery on the left spout's valve (the lab's reward block): the size, the large-reward trials and the reward
tone (src/sounds/reward_tone.bin, OpenRigs.Audio PlayRewardTone) at tone.levelDbfs, on every speaker.

sizeUl.description: Reward size, in microlitres, planned into valve pulses from the valve's calibration; at most 20, the most one reward may ask for
sizeUl.title: SizeUl

largeMultiplier.description: Reward size multiplier on large-reward trials, above 1
largeMultiplier.title: LargeMultiplier

largeProbability.description: Probability that a trial is a large-reward trial; 0: none (the only off)
largeProbability.title: LargeProbability

tone.description: The reward tone, with every reward
tone.title: Tone

Reward.title: Reward

RewardTone.description: A task's reward tone, played at each rewarded trial's levelDbfs (OpenRigs.Audio PlayRewardTone): reward.tone.

levelDbfs.description: The reward tone's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its samples outside silent stretches (runs of exactly-zero samples at least 1 ms long), as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3); mute: no sound. The lab's default mute. The workflow stops at Go if any peak at the highest level a trial can draw would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

RewardTone.title: RewardTone

SpoutsSettings.description:
The spouts (the lab's block, open_rigs.core.task Spouts; OpenRigs.Trials SpoutCommands): only the left spout counts.
Always in (this task's default): both spouts stay where Ready put them all session, as before the block. Otherwise the left
spout alone comes in at the SpoutsIn cue, stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds from the first pip (negative: before it, the trial
starting that much earlier; always in, no lead), stays in on a reward and goes out without one, and goes out
rewardConsumptionSeconds into the next interval (time to drink a reward, inside the interval; nothing while always in). A lick counts from the response window's opening (trialStructure.stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds after
the first pip), so a positive stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds is at most that (lib's Spouts.check_fits); a negative one, the
trial's lead, is in whole 50 ms steps (the pips' grid from the trial start).

alwaysIn.description: Always in: both spouts stay where Ready put them for the whole session, never moved by the task (this task's default)
alwaysIn.title: AlwaysIn

stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds.description: From stimulus onset to moving the spouts in (the SpoutsIn cue), in seconds, signed like laserToStimulusSeconds: negative, the spouts in that long before the stimulus (the trial starts that much earlier; with rewardConsumptionSeconds at most itiMinSeconds); positive, at most the stimulus to the response window's opening
stimulusToSpoutsInSeconds.title: StimulusToSpoutsInSeconds

rewardConsumptionSeconds.description: From the next interval's start (the outcome plus any timeout) to drawing the spouts out (the SpoutsOut cue), in seconds: time to drink a reward, inside the interval, which it never delays; with any lead of the spouts before the stimulus, at most itiMinSeconds
rewardConsumptionSeconds.title: RewardConsumptionSeconds

SpoutsSettings.title: SpoutsSettings

Stimulus.description:
When the tone and grating end (the lab's block, open_rigs.core.task StimulusTiming): durationSeconds from the first pip,
or responseToStimulusOffSeconds after the outcome (on a miss, the response window's end or the track's end), whichever comes
first; until then they go on following the wheel and the auto-progress after the outcome, held at the track's end. A cutoff
trial's cut stimuli stay off. Logged as stimulusOffTime (the earlier of this and a cutoff where neither stimulus plays).

durationSeconds.description: The longest the stimulus lasts from its onset, in seconds; off before the next trial's stimulus can come (the soonest outcome plus the shortest penalty timeout, 0 where a reward can come, plus itiMinSeconds). Null: no cap, the stimulus ends only responseToStimulusOffSeconds after the response (both null is refused)
durationSeconds.title: DurationSeconds

responseToStimulusOffSeconds.description: From the response (the outcome; on a miss, the response window's end or the track's end) to the stimulus off, in seconds, unless the duration ends it first: 0 (the default), off at the outcome; null, the outcome does not end it (it runs durationSeconds); at most the shortest penalty timeout (0 where a reward can come, so every trial here) plus itiMinSeconds
responseToStimulusOffSeconds.title: ResponseToStimulusOffSeconds

Stimulus.title: Stimulus

StimulusCutoff.description:
A cutoff trial: which stimuli switch off, and where (a condition sets stimuli to make its trials cutoff ones).

Each listed stimulus switches off once the mouse has run a track fraction of the trial's track (the fraction one of
trackFractions, a list field); an unlisted stimulus stays on. Everything else about the trial is unchanged, so it is still
rewarded as normal: the animal has to keep going and find the reward zone without the stimulus.

stimuli.description: The stimuli that switch off: none (an ordinary trial), auditory (the tone), visual (the grating) or both
stimuli.title: Stimuli

trackFractions.description: Where the stimuli switch off, as a fraction of the trial's track length, one drawn per trial; 1 (the default) is the track's end, so never during the trial: a cutoff condition sets its own fractions
trackFractions.title: TrackFractions

StimulusCutoff.title: StimulusCutoff

Track.description: The virtual track: its lengths, how far it moves per wheel cm and how fast it moves on its own.

lengthsCm.description: Track lengths, one drawn per trial, in track cm (the mouse runs track cm / wheelGain of wheel)
lengthsCm.title: LengthsCm

wheelGain.description: Track cm per wheel cm: the track's tone and grating move this many cm for each cm the wheel turns, so the mouse runs track length / wheelGain cm of wheel to the end
wheelGain.title: WheelGain

autoProgressPerSecond.description: Fraction of the track the tone and grating advance per second on their own from the trial start, added to what the wheel sets; 0: none. Moves the stimulus only: the track's end and the cutoff points are judged on the wheel alone
autoProgressPerSecond.title: AutoProgressPerSecond

Track.title: Track

TrialCondition.description:
One kind of trial in the mix (coen-dome-decision-making's shape): its relative weight, its condition-level values (set)
by dotted path and the lists it pairs; its trialType is derived from its contrasts and level (TRIAL_TYPES), never stored.
A list in a scalar field's cell is one value picked per trial; a list field's list (LIST_FIELDS), at any level, one entry
picked per trial. Paired lists share one picked index per trial.

weight.description: Relative draw weight: each new trial picks a condition with these as relative chances
weight.title: Weight

pairs.description: Groups of paths whose lists (the set's, else the task's) have equal length and share one picked index per trial; unpaired lists are picked independently
pairs.title: Pairs

set.description: Condition-level values by dotted path, any field but x-session-fields'; the rest are the task's
set.title: Set

TrialCondition.title: TrialCondition

TrialStructure.description:
Timing of each trial. The inter-trial interval (open_rigs.core.task Iti) runs to this trial's first tone pip, with a
quiet mouse, from the last trial's outcome when rewarded (outcome, interval; the spouts out spouts.rewardConsumptionSeconds into it)
or its outcome plus its penalty timeout when penalised (outcome, timeout, interval); trial 1: from the first clock tick after Go. The response window opens stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds
after the first tone pip, licks before it not counted, and runs responseWindowSeconds from there; null: it never closes
(optogenetics then refused, as the laser's cap is derived from it). The quiet waits count from the interval's start
(open_rigs.core.task LickQuietWait, WheelQuietWait).

wheelQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with the wheel still, in seconds, counted from the interval's start: the wheel's distance (forward and back added) over the last wheelQuietSeconds must stay within wheelQuietCm; 0: off (the only off); at most 10 s
wheelQuietSeconds.title: WheelQuietSeconds

wheelQuietCm.description: The most the wheel may move, forward and back added, within the last wheelQuietSeconds before the trial's start, in cm; 0: no movement at all; at most 20 cm
wheelQuietCm.title: WheelQuietCm

lickQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with every spout released, in seconds, counted from the interval's start and restarted by every touch and release; a held contact (a paw or chin on a spout) holds the trial's start until released, so licks for the last reward cannot carry into the next trial; 0: off; at most 10 s. It lengthens the interval only when the mouse licks late in it (quietWaitSeconds)
lickQuietSeconds.title: LickQuietSeconds

responseWindowSeconds.description: The response window, in seconds from when a lick first counts (the task says when); with no response by its end the trial is noResponse. Null or left out: no limit (a task may refuse it)
responseWindowSeconds.title: ResponseWindowSeconds

itiMinSeconds.description: Lower bound of the inter-trial interval, drawn uniformly for every trial, in seconds; the quiet waits can only lengthen it (quietWaitSeconds)
itiMinSeconds.title: ItiMinSeconds

itiMaxSeconds.description: Upper bound of the inter-trial interval, in seconds; at least itiMinSeconds
itiMaxSeconds.title: ItiMaxSeconds

stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds.description: From stimulus onset (the first tone pip) to the response window opening, in seconds; responseWindowSeconds runs from that opening, and licks before it are not counted
stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds.title: StimulusToResponseWindowSeconds

TrialStructure.title: TrialStructure

UclOpenCoenDomeNavigationTaskLogic.title: UclOpenCoenDomeNavigationTaskLogic

UclOpenCoenDomeNavigationTaskParameters.description:
Task parameters for the coen-dome-navigation corridor: the lab's blocks in the lab's order (the mix, timing, stimuli,
reward, penalty, optogenetics), then the spouts, the stimulus's end, the track, the reward zone, the wrong-lick limit and stimulus cutoff.

A lick first counts from the response window's opening, trialStructure.stimulusToResponseWindowSeconds after the trial's first tone pip. Auto-reward is given on the pip whose tone reaches the reward zone's floor (rewardZoneMinHz), no lick needed, and the trial's licks are ignored (outcomeReason rewardZoneReached); on the other trials only a lick in the zone is rewarded. A trial that runs out of time or track with the tone in the zone, or ends outside the zone, is penalised. The reward is given on the left spout's valve, planned from the valve's calibration (calibration\RewardValve-Left.json); an uncalibrated valve stops the workflow at Start.

rngSeed.description: Seed of the random number generator for these task parameters
rngSeed.title: RngSeed

curriculum.description: The Mouse Curriculum stage these values came from, the only record of the stage, filled by app-rig-control at launch; Go refuses a task whose curriculum is empty or malformed
curriculum.title: Curriculum

trialConditions.description: The trial mix: each new trial picks one condition at random with the weights as relative chances, independently of every other trial, then one of its combinations: the task's values with the condition's set over them, any field but x-session-fields', each list field one entry; its trialType, derived from its values (x-trial-types), is the trial row's. One whole value: a curriculum stage's conditions replace it; the trialConditionId column is its 0-based index
trialConditions.title: TrialConditions

visualStimulus.description: The grating: its contrasts and spatial frequencies along the track

auditoryStimulus.description: The tone sweep's pips (src/sounds/pips.bin), each played at levelDbfs

autoRewardProbability.description: Probability that a trial is an auto-reward trial, rewarded on reaching the zone's floor without a lick; 0: never, 1: every trial
autoRewardProbability.title: AutoRewardProbability

penalty.description: What a penalised trial costs by its kind (open_rigs.core.task Penalty): incorrect, a trial ending outside the zone; noResponse, one out of time or track (a miss), which this task penalises, so never null

spouts.description: When the spouts move: always in, or the left spout in before the first pip and out after the reward
spouts.title: Spouts

stimulus.description: When the tone and grating end: at the outcome, after it, or after a duration

rewardZoneMinHz.description: Lower frequency of the reward zone, in Hz, above the sweep's start (src/sounds/sweep.json)
rewardZoneMinHz.title: RewardZoneMinHz

rewardZoneMaxHz.description: Upper frequency of the reward zone, in Hz, at most the track's top (24 kHz: the sweep's start times endHz / startHz in whole numbers, src/sounds/sweep.json)
rewardZoneMaxHz.title: RewardZoneMaxHz

wrongLickLimit.description: Licks outside the zone that end the trial; 0: wrong licks never end it
wrongLickLimit.title: WrongLickLimit

stimulusCutoff.description: Which stimuli switch off part way along the track, and where

auditoryStimulus.levelDbfs mute plays no tone, so where it plays is unread

VisualStimulus.description:
The grating: its contrast, and its spatial frequency from start to end along the track on a log scale, as the tone does
(TrialLogic.cs TrialRules.Frame).

contrasts.description: Candidate grating contrasts (BonVision's Contrast, 1 full contrast), one drawn per trial; 0 shows no grating
contrasts.title: Contrasts

spatialFrequencyStartCpd.description: The grating's spatial frequency at the track's start, in cycles per degree
spatialFrequencyStartCpd.title: SpatialFrequencyStartCpd

spatialFrequencyEndCpd.description: The grating's spatial frequency at the track's end, in cycles per degree
spatialFrequencyEndCpd.title: SpatialFrequencyEndCpd
